source_excerpts.text:
For an explicit rational signed affine expression
\[
f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{K}c_i\,1_{a_i+U_i}(x),
\qquad x\in\mathbb F_2^N,
\]
the algorithm acquires the **complete translation-period space**
\[
P(f)=\{p:f(x+p)=f(x)\text{ for every }x\}.
\]

It constructs an actual matrix \(B\) with \(\ker B=P(f)\), together with an explicit quotient function \(g\) satisfying
\[
f(x)=g(Bx).
\]
The row space of \(B\) is uniquely minimal among binary linear maps determining \(f\). This is minimality of linear information; it makes no claim about arbitrary nonlinear encodings.

The decisive mechanism is **exact squared Fourier energy**. The Fourier transform of each affine indicator has an explicit affine support and sign phase. Gaussian character sums therefore compute the squared energy on any affine frequency restriction. Zero energy certifies absence of support after all cancellations. These certificates recover the span of the actual Fourier support, whose orthogonal complement is \(P(f)\), without enumerating the input domain or frequency space.

The acquisition uses polynomially many exact Gaussian operations in the explicit representation size, with rational bit costs charged. Its governing argument is preserved in :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}[AFFINE_TRANSLATION_QUOTIENT_THEOREM.tex](producer-workspace/AFFINE_TRANSLATION_QUOTIENT_THEOREM.tex).

statement: Exact Gaussian character sums compute squared Fourier energy on affine frequency restrictions of the whole rational signed expression. Zero energy detects absent support after cancellation, acquiring span(supp Fourier f), whose orthogonal complement is the full period space P(f). An actual B with ker B=P(f) is minimal among binary linear determining maps.
title: Recover semantic linear symmetries after term cancellations
